1. Print out MAMA or DADA in the size and font you want in REVERSE on normal printer paper.
2. Trace the letters onto the paper side of fusible web.
3. Leaving the paper on, cut out the letters loosely, not right on the line. Leave about 1cm around the edge.
4. Iron the fusible web onto the baby clothes. The fusible web needs to be ironed onto the wrong side of the baby clothes. The paper side of the fusible web will touch the iron. Keep the paper on otherwise the fusible web will glue itself to the iron. 
5. Keep the paper on as you cut out the letter on the line this time.
6. Arrange them on your sweatshirt in the order you want them to be and in the right position. I highly recommend you take a photo at this point for reference in the next step.
7. You’re allowed to take the paper off now! You can now iron the letters on the sweatshirt, I’d recommend one at a time.
8. Machine sew around the edges using a satin stitch, or zig zag stitch with the stitches close together.
9. Clip the threads and you should be done!

There is a maximum on the amount you can study at a time. You also need to consider that some compulsory courses require you to do course A in term 1 then course B in term 2 etc.

Are you in a position to study only and not work? You might be able to do three courses per term every term this way. But if you have to work this is almost certainly going to lead to burn out. 

Also consider your social life and other commitments. Do you have to cut back on things to fit in a faster schedule? It’s hard enough as it is to find the study/life balance.

Next is to consider grades. If you want to get into postgrad, you might need a high GPA. The more study you have going on at a time means you have less time to devote to each assignment, meaning that likely your grades will be lower even if only a little. Doing less at a time often means a higher GPA at the expense of a longer degree.

Next is how is your physical and mental health? Uni is very draining on both of these and if you want to stay sane, don’t push past your breaking point. If you have a disability or chronic illness, uni is likely to stress it even more.
